models_evaluated: CORONET (random forest regression with SHAP explanations)

links.outcome: HCP concordance with correct decisions when the model intentionally recommended wrong discharge
links.effect: In Daniel's case 65% (15/23) followed the wrong discharge recommendation; in Christine's 48% (11/23). Only 35% (CS) and 52% (CS+Exp) overrode the model.
links.quote: The results strongly suggest that for both types of output (CS and CS+Ex) HCPs over-relied in the recommendation provided by the model.

links.outcome: Effect of SHAP feature-contribution explanations on HCP understanding, trust, satisfaction, and critical understanding
links.effect: No significant change in satisfaction, trust, or understanding (CS vs CS+Exp); explanation did not change understanding of wrong recommendations for 57% and lowered it for 17%.
links.quote: The explanation did not improve satisfaction (RQ2, Fig. 7 question A), trust (RQ3, Fig. 7 questions B, C, E) nor the understanding of how the model produced the recommendation (RQ1, Fig. 7 questions D, F, G).

links.outcome: Whether explanations promote scrutiny and reduce automation bias in HCP decisions
links.effect: With explanations, decisions against the model took a median 84s vs 38s for agreeing (p<0.001); only 52% overrode the wrong recommendation with explanations vs 35% without; confirmation bias risk noted.
links.quote: On the other hand, explanations drove users to reflect longer on the decision when disagreeing with the model outcome (RQ6).

links.outcome: Human-AI team decisions with and without explanation, including overreliance on incorrect model recommendations
links.effect: Lowest concordance in cases where CORONET recommended wrong action; 35% (CS) and 52% (CS+Exp) of HCPs overrode incorrect discharge recommendations.
links.quote: Only 35% (CS scenario) and 52% (CS+Ex) HCPs took that critical perspective over the model.

links.outcome: HCP expectations about uncertainty display alongside model output
links.effect: 96% (22/23) at least slightly agreed uncertainty behind the recommendation was essential; 43% (10/23) strongly agreed. The tool did not communicate uncertainty.
links.quote: Apart from knowing why the model recommends such action, the uncertainty behind the recommendation was even more essential for the HCPs: 96% (22/23) of them at least slightly agreed, and 43% (10/23) strongly agreed, which is the highest ‘strongly agree’ proportion in the study.

unlisted_practices: Displaying SHAP feature-contribution and cohort scatter plot explanations alongside predictive scores to clinicians

links.effect: Explanations did not change understanding for 57% (13/23) and lowered understanding for 17%.
links.quote: The provided explanations did not change the level of understanding of when and why the model produces wrong recommendations for 57% (13/23) of HCPs (RQ1).

links.effect: Daniel: 65% (15/23) discharged as CORONET recommended; Christine: 48% (11/23).
links.quote: In Daniel’s case 65% (15/23) HCPs decided to discharge, as CORONET recommended, while for Christine this accounted for 48% (11/23).

links.effect: Undesirable explanation effects occurred for 17-35%; critical understanding not improved for 57%.
links.quote: Despite the general positive attitude towards explanations, for a significant set of participants (17-35%), an undesirable effect for the explanations was observed, possibly due to an increase in cognitive effort.

links.outcome: Clinician satisfaction, trust, and understanding of recommendations
links.effect: Pairwise comparison between score alone and score plus explanation showed no statistically significant change in clinician satisfaction, trust, understanding, or reassurance.
links.quote: In the pairwise comparison of responses between CS and CS+Exp scenarios, we did not find a statistically significant change in the HCPs’ attitude towards the model (i.a. satisfaction, trust, understanding, reassurance).

links.outcome: Clinician detection of incorrect AI recommendations
links.effect: When the model recommended incorrect discharge, 65% (15/23) of clinicians discharged in Daniel's case and 48% (11/23) in Christine's case.
links.quote: In Daniel’s case 65% (15/23) HCPs decided to discharge, as CORONET recommended, while for Christine this accounted for 48% (11/23).
